description: HISDAC-US, historical settlement data compilation for the conterminous United States over 200 years is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Stefan Leyk et al. Studying human settlement helps explain social processes such as urbanization and interactions between human and environmental systems but not much is known about the landscape evolution before the era of operational remote sensing technology. Coverage: national (US); published in 2018. Formats: ZIP, TXT, Raster, SQLite. The data are held in Harvard Dataverse and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 23145439. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support building-stock, asset and facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
